title: Can Machines Resonate with Humans? Evaluating the Emotional and Empathic Comprehension of LMs
findings: The paper does not contain findings related to religion. Its core findings relate to the high subjectivity and low inter-annotator agreement in judging empathic similarity between stories, which poses a significant challenge for training and evaluating language models. The authors also found that this subjectivity is independent of cultural background, as similar low agreement was observed in both English and newly collected Urdu datasets. The study suggests that closer interpersonal relationships between annotators, rather than just a shared cultural background, lead to higher agreement.

measurement_description: Not applicable. The paper does not measure any aspect of faith or religion. It measures the ability of models to comprehend and evaluate empathic similarity between narratives, with a secondary focus on how cultural and linguistic backgrounds (English vs. Urdu) affect human annotations of empathy.
